c.tagline: Montenegro's low-key capital of Ottoman lanes, river bridges, and mountain gateways.

taxi.fareNote: International ride-hailing like Uber is not established here; use local taxi firms or the domestic Tapme app. Fares are metered and cheap — make sure the meter is running.

emergency.note: 112 is Montenegro's unified emergency number reaching police, ambulance and fire.

avoid.reason: Watch bags around the markets and bus station; otherwise usual city awareness.

hood_desc: Podgorica's late-19th-century core north of the Moraca around Republic Square and the Hercegovacka pedestrian street, dense with cafes, shops, hotels and the little Ribnica river bridges; the convenient walkable base for most visitors.

The Ottoman old town on the south bank by the river confluence, with narrow lanes, the Osmanagic Mosque, the Clock Tower (Sahat Kula) and the old Ribnica bridge; the most historic quarter, quiet and atmospheric.
The planned modern district across the Moraca River, home to the landmark Millennium Bridge, wide boulevards, the Delta City mall and riverside parks; spacious and contemporary.
A calm residential neighborhood on the site of the old airport south of the center, with leafy streets, local eateries and good-value stays; suits a quieter, lived-in base.
A large residential district on the western edge, mostly local apartment blocks and family homes with everyday shops and markets; budget-friendly and authentic, a little removed from the sights.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink in Podgorica.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around 10-11:00 PM; there is no night service, so taxis fill late-night gaps.
transit.note: Podgorica has no metro, tram or urban rail; the city relies on a municipal bus network plus abundant cheap taxis. The compact center is easily walkable.
transit.pay: Pay the fare in cash to the driver on board (around €0.80-€1); there is no rechargeable smart-card system.

bus: Intercity coaches from the Main Bus Station to Niksic, Bar, Kotor, Budva and the coast
train: Montenegrin Railways from Podgorica to Bar (coast), Kolasin, Bijelo Polje and Belgrade (Serbia)

transit.m: Bus to the Main Bus Station / center (~15-45 min)
Train from the Aerodrom halt to Podgorica station (~11 min)

tip.r: Not expected; rounding up or leaving 5-10% for good service is appreciated but not required.
